Misc. Appeal No. 5174 of 2009
 United India Insurance Co.Ltd.Jabalpur
 Versus
 Smt.Sheela Bai And Others
 Appearance:
 Mr. Suresh Raj - Advocate for appellant.
 Mrs. Devika Thakur - Advocate for respondent No.1.
 With
 Misc. Appeal No. 4789 of 2009

 Versus
 Parmu Sambasia Rao And Others

 Mrs. Devika Thakur - Advocate for appellants.

 Order

These miscellaneous appeals under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 have been filed by the Insurance Company and the Claimants/Legal Representatives of the deceased respectively challenging the impugned award dated 02.09.2009 passed by the Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Katni in Claim Case No.124 of 2007.
2. MA No.5174 of 2009 has been filed by appellant - United India Insurance Co. Ltd. for setting aside/modification of the award.

Whereas, MA NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:58111 2 MA-5174-2009 No.4789 of 2009 has been filed by Claimants/Legal Representative of the deceased,
namely, Smt. Sheela Bai for enhancement of the amount of compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 3. Since, both these appeals have arisen out of the common award, therefore, they are heard together and are being disposed of by this common order.
However, for the sake of convenience, the facts are taken from MA No.5174 of 2009.

entities.text: Sheela Bai vs Parmu Sambasia Rao
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Brief facts necessary for disposal of this appeal are that on the unfortunate day of 30.06.2009,
deceased Ram Prakash Dahia, aged about 35 years working as Sub-Contractor at Simplex Co. Ltd.
was travelling in an auto-rickshaw.
His auto-rickshaw met with an accident with offending vehicle Jeep bearing no. AP 27-U-4779.
The place of accident was National Highway No.5, Village Parmaua Square, Surareddipalem, PS Tangutur, District Prakasam (AP).
The deceased died on spot because of the injuries sustained in the accident.

His wife and children being legal representatives filed claim petition claiming compensation for the death of the deceased who died because of the rash and negligent driving of Jeep bearing no. AP 27-U- 4779 by Parmu Sambasia Rao, its driver and owner.

Allowing the claim petition, the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Katni awarded them Rs.
7,98,000/- as compensation for the death of deceased Ram Prakash Dahia.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the claimants has submitted that while computing the monthly income of the deceased as Rs. 6000/- per month only at the time of his death, the learned Tribunal has not considered the Income Tax Returns filed by them for the assessment year 1998-1999.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:58111 3 MA-5174-2009
The attention of this court was also drawn on the fact that wrong multiplier has been applied and hence, a prayer has been made for enhancement of the award amount.

6. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company has submitted that the findings given by the learned Tribunal regarding monthly income of the deceased were unsustainable because the recent Income Tax Returns of the deceased was not produced by the claimants, albeit, they have produced the income tax for the period much prior to accident i.e. 1998- 1999, and thus the income of the deceased could not be determined on the basis of the Income Tax Returns.
The selection of 15 and 16 as multipliers to determine the economic loss caused to the claimants because of the death of the deceased by the Tribunal, was unjustified.

7. The counsel for the claimants reverted that in the absence of any rebuttal by the appellant-Insurance Company in response to the evidence produced by the claimants regarding deceased being Income Tax Payee at the time of his death, non-production of last Income Tax Returns, would not, in any manner, affect the determination of compensation.
The Income Tax Returns of the year 1998-1999 filed by the claimants were germane to determine the income of the deceased at the time of his death.
He submitted that the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal was on lower side compensation and enhancement in the award may be warranted.

In that,
the learned Tribunal has not committed any error in selecting 15 and 16 as multipliers to determine the dependency and economic loss caused to the claimants.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:58111 4 MA-5174-2009 8.
Considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the evidence and material produced by the claimants before the learned Tribunal.

9. The plea taken by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the learned Tribunal has erred in computing the monthly income of the deceased, on the basis of Income Tax Returns of the Smt. Sheela Bai vs Parmu Sambasia Rao on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48830341/
2 deceased pertaining to the assessment year 1998-1999, cannot, by any stretch of reasoning, be said to be irrelevant to determine the income of the deceased because the appellant-Company had not led any evidence to rebut the claimants' plea about the income of the deceased and his status as Income Tax Payee at the time of his death.

entities.text: Sheela Bai vs Parmu Sambasia Rao
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the absence of any evidence or suggestion by the appellant-Company regarding either any decrease in the income of the deceased or he was ceased to be the Income Tax Payee, the Income Tax Returns placed on record for the assessment year 1998-1999 could not be ignored while consideration.

The evidence produced by the claimants on the income of the deceased member of the family having thus remained un- rebutted and the computation of the income of the deceased at the time of his death by the learned Tribunal requires reconsideration.

10. There is, however, no merit in the submission of the learned counsel for the claimants that the learned Tribunal has committed an error in selecting the multipliers to determine the claimants'
dependency on the income of the deceased.

This is so because while selecting the multiplier, the learned Tribunal appears to have taken note of the observations of the Hon'ble Supreme Court made in the case of Smt. Sarla Verma and others NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:58111 5 MA-5174-2009 versus Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in 2009(6) SCC 121 ,
where multipliers for different age groups have been suggested to ensure uniformity in selection of the multipliers by the learned Tribunals.

entities.text: Smt. Sarla Verma and others NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:58111 5 MA-5174-2009 versus Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in 2009(6) SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the age of the deceased as 35 years at the time of death, the multiplier of 16 is rightly adopted in terms of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgment referred to hereinabove.
11. Be that as it may, the claimants, have brought on record, income tax return of year 1998-1999 marked as Exhibit P/18 to prove the income of the deceased.
No specific rebuttal has been brought on record by the other side to disprove this averment in respect of Exhibit P/18.
A bare perusal of Exhibit P/18 makes it clear that the annual income assessed was Rs.1,04,784/- in the year 1998-1999 which comes to Rs.8,732/- per month.
The deceased was also holder of PAN card.

It is of common knowledge that a person who is regularly working in the same field will start earning more,
as time passes and as he gets more and more experienced.
The income tax return can be given a go-bye.
In the considered opinion of this court, in the present facts and circumstances of the case the monthly income of the deceased is required to be considered as Rs.10,000/- per month.

Therefore, the annual income of the deceased considering as Rs.1,20,000/- after deducting 1/3rd for his personal and living expenses and applying multiplier of 16, the total dependency of the claimants would be Rs.12,80,000/-.
12.

The findings of the learned Tribunal in the award on Issues No.2 and 3 are, therefore, required to be modified and loss of dependency of the claimants on the income of the deceased is determined afresh.
No other NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:58111 6 MA-5174-2009 heads are required to be enhanced.

13. The award of the learned Tribunal made in Claim Petition No.124/2007 is accordingly modified enhancing the compensation towards loss of dependency as Rs. 12,80,000/- in place of Rs.
7,68,000/-.
The amount so awarded in the other heads be as it is.
The enhanced compensation shall carry same interest as has been awarded by learned Tribunal.

Therefore, the amount awarded by the Smt. Sheela Bai vs Parmu Sambasia Rao on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48830341/

 dependency  Loss of estate Rs.5,000/- Rs.5,000/-
 Funeral expenses Rs.5,000/- Rs.5,000/-
 Loss of  Rs.10,000/- Rs.10,000/-
 consortium  Transportation Rs.10,000/- Rs.10,000/-

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in view of the foregoing discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that the award passed by the learned Tribunal warrants interference to enhance the compensation from Rs.7,98,000/- to Rs.13,10,000/-.
The enhanced amount comes to Rs.5,12,000/- (Rs.13,10,000 - Rs.7,98,000) which shall carry same interest as awarded by the Tribunal.
Rest of the conditions as imposed by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

14. In view of the foregoing discussion, Misc. Appeal No.4789/2009 stands partly allowed and the impugned award is modified to the extent indicated herein above subject to following conditions:-
i.

The respondent No.3 is directed to deposit the compensation NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:58111 7 MA-5174-2009 amount within 60 days from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be taken out against him.
ii. The claimant is directed to pay the requisite Court Fee, if required in the present case.
iii. On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest and costs, by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
iv. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.
v. As a sequel, interlocutory applications pending consideration, if any, shall stand closed 15.
The ground raised by the appellant/insurance company sans merit and are hereby discarded.
The appeal filed by the insurance company being M.A. No.5174/2009 is hereby dismissed .
Insurance company is directed to indemnify the claimants within a period of eight weeks from the date of passing of this order.
16. These appeals are, accordingly, disposed of.
No order as to cost.
